Forwarding MerchantPay's note and the attachments they provided. Key facts: they claim EU VAT registration (DE) and request reverse-charge treatment on invoice #1234. Payment run is scheduled for June 5. I asked for confirmation of the VAT number and preferred invoicing flow, but want to confirm our risk posture before I commit to reissuing:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: VAT treatment on monthly invoice — quick internal triage (MerchantPay)

Ben / Hannah —

Quick finance view:

- Do not delay the merchant's payment run on our side. We should not withhold funds unilaterally.
- Operational flow: validate the VAT ID via VIES immediately. If VIES returns valid and the business classification looks like B2B, proceed to reissue a corrected invoice net of VAT and include the EU reverse-charge wording: "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Article 44 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC."
- Require merchant to upload the VAT certificate and provide the exact VAT number string. Take a screenshot of the VIES hit and store with the invoice.
- If VIES fails, request additional evidence (registration letter or local tax office confirmation). In that case we keep VAT on the original invoice and escalate to tax for guidance before any credit/reissue.

Tax sign-off: for standard B2B reverse-charge reissues described above, finance can proceed without tax sign-off, but escalate if there are red flags (multiple country residency claims, inconsistent registration address, or unusually high invoice split).

Action items for Ben: validate VAT number (VIES), ask merchant whether they want Redwood to reissue or whether they will self-bill. If they ask Redwood to reissue, create a corrected invoice and attach VIES screenshot and their certificate to the transaction record.

I've attached the internal checklist for VAT reverse-charge handling for reference.

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the prompt info. Here are the agreed next steps and timeline so we can complete this before your payment run: 

1) Please confirm the VAT number exactly as you want it validated (e.g., DE123456789). We received your certificate but need the exact string for VIES.
2) If validated via VIES, Redwood will reissue invoice #1234 net of VAT and include the EU reverse-charge statement. We will attach the VIES lookup screenshot and your certificate to the transaction record.
3) If you prefer to self-bill, confirm and provide the self-billed invoice PDF with the reverse-charge note and we will accept that instead of a Redwood reissue.
4) Target: we can reissue the corrected invoice within 24 business hours of receiving the VAT number confirmation. Please send before end of day Jun 2 to make the June 5 payment run.

For transparency, finance (Marissa) confirmed we won't withhold funds; we'll remediate the invoice and amend records if VIES validates. If VIES does not validate we will request supporting evidence and escalate to our tax team.
